units.translation: Once again reference is made to ⟦1⟧ 823, but this is denied only very briefly; then she asks them to desist from their threats and from carrying them out, in the course of which she too uses a mild threat (which also has its effect), and finally repeats her promises.
⟦1⟧ (only here) must have been formed after the already Homeric ⟦2⟧ (= ⟦3⟧); Weil writes ⟦4⟧ from ⟦5⟧ 817.
⟦1⟧: of the poor mortals, who are powerless against you goddesses.

826 ⟦1⟧ formula of passing over something when one considers it superfluous to say (⟦2⟧, ⟦3⟧, ⟦4⟧ C ⟦5⟧; ⟦6⟧), or avoids it for another reason (⟦7⟧), as here too Athena deliberately holds back the threat. See Paley. Athena, however, becomes somewhat more explicit. With 827 f. one compares ⟦8⟧, where Athena says of Zeus: ⟦9⟧, ⟦10⟧. —
for it would have been no advantage to me
but he says he will give me the thunderbolt
to hurl at the Achaeans and burn their ships with fire
829 ⟦1⟧ (so also here in the manuscripts): see on ⟦2⟧. —

830 ⟦1⟧ ⟦2⟧ ⟦3⟧⟦4⟧; yet here ⟦5⟧ is more 'wicked', 'evil', cf. 337, ⟦6⟧. 762, ⟦7⟧ ⟦8⟧, Aeschylus. ⟦9⟧ ⟦10⟧; so Wakefield's conjecture seems correct so far, and also ⟦11⟧ is easier to understand than ⟦12⟧, which, like the dative, would have to be construed with what follows, as subject accusative to ⟦13⟧.
⟦1⟧ so metaphorically ⟦2⟧ ⟦3⟧. From the ⟦4⟧ have now, less mythically, become curses.
if there will be fruit according to the oracles of Loxias
⟦1⟧ 832 follows asyndetically according to the manuscripts; but also ⟦2⟧ aorist (⟦3⟧) is absolutely expected, unless one writes before it 830 ⟦4⟧: refrain from curses, and then calm yourself further.
⟦1⟧ like Homer µ 169 ⟦2⟧; also ⟦3⟧ (on 651) remains within the metaphor.
and a god lulled the waves to sleep
— 834 ⟦1⟧ namely ⟦2⟧; so the sacrifices will be numerous.

⟦1⟧ 'great, wide', like ⟦2⟧ ⟦3⟧ ⟦4⟧⟦5⟧. What is attested here is (cf. Schol.) that to the ⟦6⟧ first-fruit offerings (of grain) were brought for marriage and fertility of children, ⟦7⟧ (Schol.; Plato Laws VI 774 E), in which they appear as earth-goddesses similar to Demeter, Preller-Robert Myth. 841.
⟦1⟧ Ag. 1409, ⟦2⟧ (Homer Z 270); Hesychius explains ⟦3⟧ with †⟦4⟧ (⟦5⟧⟨⟦6⟧⟩⟦7⟧?), ⟦8⟧, yet with the concept of ⟦9⟧ (properly burnt offering) that of ⟦10⟧ has also been extended.
